queries: Anthropic Fable model sluggish demand Financial Times

sources_considered.why: Summarizes the FT/Ramp report on Fable 5 spending share.
Reports July 2026 demand for Fable 5 exceeding Anthropic's compute capacity.
Paywalled FT original; only secondary summaries were available.

receipt.public_excerpt: corporate spending on Claude Fable 5 has stagnated and is not increasing significantly. This suggests that some companies may be starting to think that they don't necessarily need to use the top-of-the-line AI model

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms the FT/Ramp report he cites: Fable 5 spending flattened, and buyers chose cheaper models. This is context for his impression, not a scored outcome.

receipt.public_excerpt: Fable 5 is its most powerful model, the one subscribers have been demanding en masse since launch, to the point of saturating the company's computing capacity.

evidence_items.explanation: In July, demand for Fable 5 exceeded Anthropic's capacity. That cuts against a literal 'dead on arrival' reading, though it predates the plateau.

unresolved_gaps: The FT original was paywalled and could not be read directly.
No firm threshold exists against which to score 'dead on arrival'.
